In recent weeks, ChatGPT users have only been subject to weekly usage limits, but OpenAI announced today (the 25th) that it will restore the five-hour usage limits for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Details are as follows.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers will see the five-hour usage cap restored

OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT engineering lead Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux announced tonight (the 25th) that, starting tomorrow (the 26th), the five-hour usage limit will be restored for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

Once a user hits the five-hour or weekly usage cap, they can wait for the next cycle to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also periodically reset usage for users at no cost; users can earn reserved reset credits through designated promotional events and referral offers.

However, in recent weeks OpenAI had temporarily lifted the five-hour usage limits on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly cap in place.

During that period, the company also reset users' weekly allowances ahead of schedule on several occasions to celebrate milestones — including these two (now merged) platforms collectively reaching one million additional active users.

That said, as Tibo explained on X tonight (the 25th):

"We will restore the five-hour limit for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex tomorrow. I mentioned this before, and it was later postponed. We have to do this because: (1) the five-hour limit helps us spread out the compute load and makes the weekly allowance more generous; (2) most Plus plan users are lighter, newer users who sometimes unknowingly burn through their entire weekly allowance and then feel confused — that's not a good experience. Over the coming months, the US$100 and US$200 Pro subscriptions will continue to have no five-hour limit."

Tibo made no mention of any changes to Enterprise or Education accounts, which currently use a separate credits-based usage system.

Does the return of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
